gates.note: The catalogue is one of this gate's own consumers, so editing scripts/GATES.md reddens the gate that documents it.

Diff-scoped: its findings are relative to the resolved base ref, so `main` moving is a real input even when no file changed. `.gitignore` and `.git/info/exclude` decide which untracked modules it treats as changed.
Shares check-proof-recipes.py with gate 3 but runs its --duplication branch, which returns before the generator check; the recipe registry and generated surfaces are NOT its inputs.
The baseline seals sha256 of the registry file's bytes, so any byte change to proof-residue-registry.json reddens the gate until --write-baseline.

The wrapper always passes --negative-controls, which copies the whole tree six times. Only the lift manifest and the Blanc corpus can change the verdict; the copy reads every other file but cannot draw a conclusion from one. A whole-tree membership population was tried here and removed: the failure it was meant to catch is a file becoming unreadable, which changes no membership, so it bought no soundness and invalidated the gate whenever any unrelated file was added. A copy that fails exits nonzero, and a nonzero run is never cached.

The falsifier harness copies the whole scripts/reference/weth10 tree per coordinated case, but only the input files named here are ever loaded back out of the copy. The four WETH10_REFERENCE_*/WETH10_COMPATIBILITY_DOC overrides repoint the lock, the vendored input tree and the compatibility document, so they are inputs even though they are normally unset.

The pinned input tree is membership-sensitive: the generator requires its sorted relative-path list to equal its own table, so adding or removing a file under scripts/reference/lido-circuit-breaker fails the gate. The two REFERENCE_* variables redirect the tree and the lock, so they are declared; a run held at such an override reads files this entry does not fingerprint.

gates.reason: Lake's own incremental build already selects exactly the modules whose inputs moved, and it is what makes every depHash this registry reads current. It is executed before planning, at every run, and is never credited from a record.

gates.note: std-json-input.json is assembled inline from the repository root rather than from a module constant, so it is the easiest read in the profiler to miss. The baseline ledger is sha256-pinned inside the schema module and has no write mode.
The shadow scan indexes every .lean file under Blanc/ and scripts/, not merely the imports today's fixtures choose, so a new first-party Lean file anywhere in either tree can change the verdict.

The gate refuses to start unless the owner's .olean is already built; the fixture entry's Lake depHash witnesses that artifact, so no build path is declared separately. The owner is also read as text for its header pins.

The axiom probe imports all thirty-one owner modules, four of which (absent, unregister, unregisterWorld, unregisterAttainment) are outside the fixture's import closure, so the modules are declared alongside the fixture entry. The same thirty-one files are read as text for their header pins.

With the Chain owner ACTIVE the gate reads the working Chain source and never shells out to git; git is reachable only on --chain-dry-run, which this command does not pass. Blanc/LidoCircuitBreaker.lean is read but never pinned — the dispatcher inventory is derived from it, so its bytes still decide the verdict.

The fixture generator importlib-loads gen-weth-fixtures.py for its EEST helpers; it never calls build_fixture, so the EEST template that file names is not read and is not declared. AxiomCheck.lean is elaborated by check.sh and separately read as text by both check.sh and the deployment checker, and the Lean entry already covers its bytes. The pinned EELS checkout gitignores its own virtualenv, so the commit identity `external` proves says nothing about which coincurve, ethereum_rlp or ethereum_types is installed there. The interpreter and every installed package's METADATA are fingerprinted directly, through the same EELS_ROOT the gate itself resolves.

check-extraction-ownership.py is importlib-loaded for its declaration parser alone, so editing that parser flips this verdict with nothing else moving. The gate pins exact Lean diagnostic text, which is why the toolchain is a declared input rather than only a build dependency; the raw-commit mutants are derived from the fixture at run time and are outputs.

This gate runs check-execution-settlement.py and check-execution-raw-attribution-ownership.py as subprocesses and asserts on their verdict prefixes, so gate 21's whole closure is a subset of this one's; both nested OK lines are captured rather than printed, so only the occurrence verdict reaches stdout. Its sole-owner scan walks Blanc/**/*.lean and its manifest globs Blanc/Weth10*.lean and Blanc/Lido*.lean, so membership of the Blanc corpus is load-bearing and the recursive population covers all of it.

check-layering.py is importlib-loaded for its CONTRACTS literal, which decides which contract modules this gate audits — gate 24 regex-scrapes the same file as text, so the two couple to it by different mechanisms and a formatting change breaks only one of them. The mutant and deletion fixtures are generated from CycleWriteFreeRegression.lean at run time and need no declaration of their own.

The owner manifest SHA-256-pins the implementation, fixtures and manifests of gates 21, 22 and 23 plus lakefile.lean and lake-manifest.json, so editing any of those reddens this gate; every pinned path is declared here. It also folds every public declaration header in Blanc/Weth*.lean into one aggregate, so adding or removing such a file fails the gate — the recursive Blanc population is what preserves that membership sensitivity.

The harness is run with `lake env lean --run`, unlike the #eval evaluators elsewhere in this family.
The 606-row expectation table lives inline in check.sh, so the wrapper's own bytes are a verdict input alongside the elaborated AxiomCheck.lean.
The pinned inventory count lives in the wrapper, so its bytes are an input.

Composed specialist: its own module-level selector decides what to measure, and this outer fingerprint is the union of what that selector consumes — the whole Lean corpus, the shared Lean/Lake configuration, the Lake-recorded artifact identity of both roots, its baseline, and its own implementation. A reused row therefore means the selector would itself have measured nothing.

--no-build skips `lake build jaune/jaune`, so the prebuilt Jaune runner binary is the thing that produces PASS/FAIL and is fingerprinted directly. weth10-reference.py and weth10_reference_schema.py are in the closure only because the borrower checker importlib-loads the former for its keccak256.
This suite has no manifest, so its fixture-directory membership is its only population guard; declaring the population here restores that guard for reuse decisions.
